title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) placed on injured reserve
items.desc: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been placed on injured reserve and will be sidelined for at least four weeks.
items.impact: The Jets are placing their first-round rookie on injured reserve after he suffered an ankle injury in his NFL debut last week. He is going to miss at least four weeks as a result, but he's not expected to be out much beyond that. Adonai Mitchell and Kenyon Sadiq will both see increased opportunities in his absence for the next few weeks at least.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kene Nwangwu (back) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Kene Nwangwu (back) won't play in Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Nwangwu missed New York's season opener last week due to injury, and he is now set to miss another game on Sunday due to a back issue that he's dealing with. His absence won't have much of an impact on New York's offense, as he is relegated to more of a special teams role for the Jets.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Will McDonald IV (ankle) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Will McDonald IV (ankle) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: McDonald will officially carry a questionable tag for Sunday's game after suffering a minor ankle injury during the week. It looks like he will be cleared to play in time, however, as HC Aaron Glenn told reporters that the veteran edge rusher should be available to play against the Packers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Troy Franklin (knee) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Troy Franklin (knee) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
items.impact: Franklin found himself on the injury report earlier in the week due to a knee issue, but he was able to practice in full all week and will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Marvin Mims Jr. (foot) unavailable for Sunday
items.desc: Marvin Mims Jr. (foot) will be unavailable for Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
items.impact: Mims is going to be sidelined in Week 2 after recently suffering a foot injury of some kind. He wasn't very involved on Denver's offense in the season opener, so his absence isn't expected to make much of an impact from a fantasy perspective.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: RJ Harvey (hamstring) is officially questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
items.impact: Harvey will go into the weekend with a questionable tag after missing practice earlier in the week due to a hamstring injury. It looks like he's trending towards playing on Sunday, but if he's ruled out ahead of game time, fantasy managers should expect rookie Jonah Coleman to see increased opportunities against Jacksonville in his absence.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) cleared to play Sunday
items.desc: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Thomas suffered a shoulder injury during the team's season opener last week, but he was able to practice all week and won't miss any time because of it. He has been cleared to play on Sunday and should continue to contribute in his usual capacity for the Jaguars for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cole Van Lanen (knee) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: Cole Van Lanen (knee) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Van Lanen's knee injury is nothing more than a minor issue at this point and won't stop him from playing on Sunday. Jacksonville's offensive line should be at full strength in Week 2, which is good news ahead of a tough matchup against Denver's stout defensive front.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Foyesade Oluokun (wrist) will play Sunday
items.desc: Foyesade Oluokun (wrist) will play in Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Jacksonville has cleared Oluokun to play in their matchup against Denver on Sunday. That's good news for the team, as he is one of their key defenders and will be needed in what projects to be a close matchup in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) set to play Sunday
items.desc: LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) is set to play in Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: To no surprise, Allen has received full clearance and will again be available to play on Sunday. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to get much work behind Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. in this matchup, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Meyers was on the injury report all week due to a lingering wrist issue, but he is going to be good to go and will play in Sunday's game against the Broncos. Fantasy managers shouldn't trust in his week-to-week consistency at this point in the season, however, especially in what projects to be a tough matchup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Aidan O'Connell (personal) listed questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Aidan O'Connell (personal) is listed as questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: O'Connell may not be able to play on Sunday due to a personal issue of some kind that he's managing right now. He is currently Las Vegas' QB3, however, so his absence wouldn't have a notable impact on their lineup.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Aaron Donald plans to play in Week 2
items.desc: Aaron Donald expects to play Monday night against the Giants.
items.impact: According to head coach Sean McVay, at the start of this week, Donald was still uncertain to play Monday night. Donald made it known after Friday's practice session that he intends to be in action. The future Hall of Famer has not appeared in an NFL game since December 31, 2023.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Lukas Van Ness (concussion) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Lukas Van Ness (concussion) is questionable for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
items.impact: The Packers are uncertain whether or not Van Ness will play on Sunday, as he has yet receive full clearance from the NFL's concussion protocols. His absence would mean a weaker defensive front this week in a matchup against Breece Hall and the Jets.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) listed questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) is listed as questionable to play in Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
items.impact: A knee injury may leave Bako-Bewele sidelined on Sunday, as he is officially considered questionable heading into the weekend. Aaron Banks (knee) is also uncertain to play, so Green Bay's offensive line may be much weaker than usual if both of those guys are ruled out ahead of game time.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Aaron Banks (knee) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Aaron Banks (knee) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
items.impact: Banks has yet to make his season debut due to a knee injury, and it's threatening to leave him sidelined for another game on Sunday. Green Bay is dealing with multiple offensive line injuries right now, so they could be weaker than usual against the Jets this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Max Melton (ankle) considered questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Max Melton (ankle) is considered questionable for Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.
items.impact: The Cardinals may be without a key defender on Sunday, as Melton is considered questionable to play due to his ankle injury. His absence would make life easier for Drew Lock, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and Seattle's offense as a whole this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tory Horton (hamstring) without injury designation for Sunday
items.desc: Tory Horton (hamstring) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: There was never much doubt surrounding Horton's availability for Week 2, but he has now received official clearance and will be available to suit up against the Cardinals. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cooper Kupp (back) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: Cooper Kupp (back) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: The veteran wideout was limited at practice earlier in the week due to a back injury, but he is over it now and carries no injury designation heading into the weekend. He doesn't project to be a good fantasy option in this matchup, however, especially with Drew Lock set to start at quarterback for the Seahawks this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Emmanwori was not able to play in Seattle's season opener last week, but he may make his season debut on Sunday, as he is officially considered questionable to play at this point. His return would provide a nice boost to this already-elite defense in a divisional matchup against the Cardinals.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jordan Whittington (quad) added to injury report Friday
items.desc: Jordan Whittington (quad) was added to the injury report as a non-participant on Friday.
items.impact: Whittington is at risk of being sidelined in Week 2 after missing Friday's practice due to a quad injury of some kind. Puka Nacua (hip) is also at risk of being sidelined now, so fantasy managers should pay close attention to updates about the health of these two receivers prior to Monday night's game.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Puka Nacua (hip) doesn't practice Friday
items.desc: Puka Nacua (hip) was added to the injury report as a non-participant at practice on Friday.
items.impact: Nacua is a new addition to the injury report, being listed with a hip injury of some kind that left him sidelined from practice on Friday. This is a situation that fantasy managers should be closely monitoring heading into the weekend because it could lead to him being limited or sidelined against the Giants on Monday night, which would be devastating for many managers relying on him for a big game at the end of the week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Eddy Pineiro (illness) uncertain to play Sunday
items.desc: Eddy Pineiro (illness) is uncertain to play in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: The veteran kicker is officially considered questionable to play heading into the weekend. He is dealing with a mildly serious illness right now that has left him sidelined from practice all week, and it's unclear whether or not he will be ready to go in time for the team's matchup against the Dolphins, which would make them need to determine who will take his place prior to kickoff.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kaelon Black (groin) questionable to play Sunday
items.desc: Kaelon Black (groin) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: The rookie was added to the injury report due to a groin issue on Thursday and will officially be questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Dolphins. He was quite involved in San Francisco's season opener last week, so his absence would likely lead to Christian McCaffrey seeing a supermajority of touches for the team in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kyle Juszczyk (finger) available for Sunday
items.desc: Kyle Juszczyk (finger) will be available for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: The 49ers will have their star fullback for Sunday's game against Miami. He won't have any fantasy relevance himself but should help open things up for RB Christian McCaffrey in this favorable matchup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: George Kittle (Achilles) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: George Kittle (Achilles) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: As expected, Kittle carries no injury designation heading into the weekend and will be available to play against the Dolphins. It seems likely that he will continue to be limited in some capacity, though it looks like the 49ers are planning on ramping his workload up more and more each week moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Alec Pierce (heel) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Alec Pierce (heel) will be good to go for Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Pierce missed Indianapolis' practice on Thursday, but it looks like that was just for injury maintenance, as he was back and a full participant for them at practice on Friday. He carries no injury designation heading into the weekend and will play on Sunday night, although it remains quite possible that he will continue to have minor limitations while the team ramps his workload back up.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Anthony Richardson Sr. (groin) active for Week 2
items.desc: Anthony Richardson Sr. (groin) will be active for Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Richardson is going to be active for the Colts on Sunday night, so his groin injury is likely considered nothing more than a minor issue at this point. He will continue to serve as the QB2 for this team behind Daniel Jones.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) set to play Sunday
items.desc: Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) is set to play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: Neither of DeJean's injuries are serious at this point and he goes into the weekend without an injury designation. He will continue to play a big role on Philadelphia's defense moving forward, assuming he suffers no setbacks with his recovery.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jonathan Greenard (pec) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Jonathan Greenard (pec) won't play play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: The veteran edge rusher is going to be out this week, despite taking part at practice all week. He should return to the lineup and provide a nice boost to Philly's pass rush sometime in the near future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen Carter (wrist) available to play Sunday
items.desc: Jalen Carter (wrist) will be available to play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
items.impact: Philadelphia's defense gets some good news ahead of Sunday's game, with Carter receiving full clearance to play against the Titans. He should continue to be a game-wrecker in what projects to be an easy matchup against Tennessee's low-powered offense.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Daron Payne (knee) cleared to play Sunday
items.desc: Daron Payne (knee) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: Payne now has full clearance to play in Sunday's game against the Cowboys, which was to be expected after he was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday. Look for his presence to make a positive impact on Washington's defensive front in this matchup and beyond.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Ladd McConkey (ribs) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Ladd McConkey (ribs) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders due to a rib injury.
items.impact: McConkey was a DNP Wednesday and Thursday but got back on the practice field Friday. His chances to play are more on the slim side, but if he plays, you need to start him against this Raiders defense. If he sits, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris are next in line for targets.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Javon Kinlaw (back) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Javon Kinlaw (back) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
items.impact: Kinlaw returned to practice on Friday and will officially be questionable to play in Washington's matchup against Dallas on Sunday. Their defensive front will be a little short on depth if he is ruled out ahead of kickoff for this game.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Odafe Oweh (calf) available to play Sunday
items.desc: Odafe Oweh (calf) will be available to play in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: As expected, Oweh is going to be available to play through his minor calf injury on Sunday. The team will need him to step up and help anchor down the defensive front in what projects to be a tough matchup against the Cowboys.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jaylin Lane (groin) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Jaylin Lane (groin) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: A groin injury left Lane limited at practice all week, but it's not a serious issue and won't affect his availability for Sunday's game against Dallas. He doesn't project to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: K'Lavon Chaisson (knee) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: K'Lavon Chaisson (knee) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: Chaisson will be available to play on Sunday after managing a knee issue at practice throughout the week. He will continue to play an important role for the Commanders in their divisional matchup against Dallas' talented offense.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Greg Newsome II (rib) again limited on Friday
items.desc: Greg Newsome II (rib) was again a limited participant at practice on Friday.
items.impact: Newsome was limited for a second-straight practice on Friday as he continues to battle a rib injury of some kind. Deonte Banks (calf) and Paulson Adebo (Knee/IR) are both injured members of New York's secondary as well, so they may be much thinner than usual in Monday night's tough matchup against the Rams.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Deonte Banks (calf) downgraded to non-participant Friday
items.desc: Deonte Banks (calf) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Friday.
items.impact: Banks was not able to practice on Friday after being limited by a calf injury on Thursday. It looks like he's trending the wrong way for Week 2, which is bad news for the Giants, considering that they are dealing with multiple key injuries in their secondary.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Andrew Thomas (ankle) limited again Friday
items.desc: Andrew Thomas (ankle) was limited at practice again on Friday.
items.impact: The star offensive lineman has been limited at two-straight practices to start the week. It looks like he's trending towards playing on Monday night, assuming he suffers no setbacks between now and then.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: B.J. Hill (Achilles) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: B.J. Hill (Achilles) is questionable for the Bengals game against the Texans on Sunday.
items.impact: Hill was not in uniform during the teams practice, so it's unlikely he plays this weekend. He'll have to wait another week to see the field.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cedric Gray (concussion) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Cedric Gray (concussion) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia eagles.
items.impact: Gray has been a full participant at practice all week but still has yet to officially the NFL's concussion protocols, so he will be questionable to play in Week 2. His absence would be bad news for Tennessee's defense in a matchup against the Eagles this week.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Joe Burrow (back) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Joe Burrow (back) is questionable for the Bengals game against the Texans due to a back injury. Burrow has told the media he would play.
items.impact: The questionable tag is likely a formality given Burrows limited practice status throughout the week. He should be fine and good to go against a Texans defense that just got bulldozed by the Bills.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Sean Tucker (hamstring) available to play for Sunday
items.desc: Sean Tucker (hamstring) will be available to play in Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.
items.impact: As expected, Tucker is back near full health and is going to be available to play against the Browns on Sunday. He is expected to be squarely behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell in the team's pecking order, however, making him irrelevant for fantasy purposes.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen McMillan (knee) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Jalen McMillan (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.
items.impact: McMillan was able to practice in a full capacity all week, but he still hasn't received full clearance to play and is officially questionable heading into the weekend. If he's unable to suit up this week, look for rookie Ted Hurst III to see more work as a result of his absence.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
items.impact: Jeudy is going to be good to go on Sunday, which was expected after he was able to practice without limitations this week. He isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for however long Deshaun Watson is starting for the Browns, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Elgton Jenkins (back) cleared to play for Sunday
items.desc: Elgton Jenkins (back) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
items.impact: Jenkins will be available to play on Sunday despite being on the injury report recently due to a back injury. Tevin Jenkins (back) has been ruled out for Cleveland, however, so their offensive line will still be at less than full power against the Buccaneers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) ruled out for Sunday
items.desc: Nico Collins (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
items.impact: Collins recently suffered a hamstring injury and will not be able to play in Sunday's game as a result. It may cause him to miss more time beyond this game as well, but we likely won't know more about his official recovery timeline until later this week or next. Look for Dalton Schultz, Kayshon Boutte, and Jaylin Noel to see more work as a result of his absence against the Bengals in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Darnell Washington (personal) set to play Sunday
items.desc: Darnell Washington (personal) is set to play in Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
items.impact: Washington missed two practices while tending to a personal issue earlier in the week, but he carries no designation heading into the weekend and will be available to play against the Patriots. He doesn't project to have fantasy relevance for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Troy Fautanu (ankle) listed questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Troy Fautanu (ankle) is listed questionable for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
items.impact: The Steelers are at risk of playing without their starting left tackle on Sunday, as Fautanu is currently questionable to play due to an ankle injury. His absence would be a big hit to Pittsburgh's offense in an already-tough road matchup in Week 2.
